claims.title: External sign-in flooding can deny identity-broker service
claims.description: An attacker operating from outside `boundary:corporate-network` can repeatedly drive sign-in attempts through `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in` to the internet-facing `process:identity-broker`. Each attempt makes the broker handle a sign-in and consult `store:directory`; successful attempts also cause token issuance and a write on `flow:identity-broker-to-audit-log:write-sign-ins`. If rate limits, request-size/concurrency bounds, and load shedding are not present, the attacker spends inexpensive client requests to exhaust the broker's workers, CPU, connections, or its dependent store capacity. Second-order, `process:identity-broker` is the shared sign-in chokepoint for colleagues and is also queried by `process:store-admin-console` over `flow:store-admin-console-to-identity-broker:fetch-public-key`; saturation prevents legitimate sign-ins and can disrupt applications' token-validation dependency. This is conditional on the model-silent capacity and overload controls, not an assertion that they are absent.

grounds.text: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because `process:identity-broker` is `internet-facing` and `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in` crosses from `boundary:outside-corporate-network`, while the flow's authentication state is `unknown` and overload controls are not specified. Impact is high because `process:identity-broker` is tagged `availability-critical`, is the stated sign-in path for colleague-used applications, and its failure also affects the `process:store-admin-console` dependency that fetches its public key.

mitigations.summary: Apply identity-aware rate limits and bounded sign-in concurrency
mitigations.detail: At `process:identity-broker`, rate-limit sign-in attempts per verified account and source, cap concurrent authentication work, and shed excess requests before directory reads, token signing, and audit writes.

mitigations.summary: Bound downstream work and isolate shared dependencies
mitigations.detail: Set short timeouts and bounded connection pools for `flow:identity-broker-to-directory:read-write-directory` and `flow:identity-broker-to-audit-log:write-sign-ins`; use backpressure or durable buffering so audit latency cannot consume all broker capacity.

mitigations.summary: Protect relying applications from broker overload
mitigations.detail: Use cached public-key material with bounded refresh and timeouts on `flow:store-admin-console-to-identity-broker:fetch-public-key`, so a broker flood does not immediately block token validation by `process:store-admin-console`.

claims.title: A store manager can administer every store rather than only their own
claims.description: An authenticated colleague holding a legitimate store-manager token can use `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void` against `process:store-admin-console` for stores other than their assigned store. The console authorizes solely from the group in the token and does not bind the action to the colleague's store, so the caller escalates from authority over one store to price changes and transaction voids across every store. The request enters the corporate zone on `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void`; the terminal capability is alteration of financial and business-critical operations at any store.

grounds.text: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions. The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because any authenticated store manager can submit the ordinary write request over `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void`, which crosses into the corporate zone, and needs only to choose another store. Impact is high because `process:store-admin-console` and its inbound flow are tagged `financial` and `business-critical-data`, and the unauthorized authority covers every store.

mitigations.summary: Enforce store-scoped authorization at the console
mitigations.detail: Have `process:store-admin-console` derive the colleague's permitted store scope from the verified token subject and enforce it server-side for every price-change and void operation; reject caller-supplied or unbound store identifiers.

mitigations.summary: Issue store-scoped roles or grants
mitigations.detail: Replace the global store-manager group decision with a role or entitlement bound to specific stores, using deny-by-default authorization for stores not present in that entitlement.

claims.title: Store managers may deny price changes and transaction voids because no action record is identified
claims.description: A colleague using `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void` can change prices or void transactions at `process:store-admin-console`, including against any store. The model identifies `store:audit-log` only as receiving sign-ins from `process:identity-broker`; it identifies no change-history or security-event record that binds these console actions to the token's staff ID. If no such record exists outside the described model, a legitimate store-manager can perform a disputed price change or void and deny it, while the operator cannot rebut the denial with attributable evidence. This is conditional on confirming whether the console emits an immutable audit record containing actor, action, target, timestamp, and outcome. Second-order: disputes affect financial and business-critical actions across every store reachable through the console.

claims.title: Compromise of the internet-facing identity broker becomes authority to issue tokens for every application

rejected_claims.title: A former or demoted manager can retain cross-store authority for up to twelve hours
rejected_claims.description: A colleague who legitimately held the store-manager group before removal can retain and present their already-issued token on `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void`. Because `process:store-admin-console` accepts the token alone, does not call back to `process:identity-broker`, and the broker cannot revoke the twelve-hour token before expiry, the former manager continues to exercise authority after their group membership or employment should no longer permit it. Combined with the console's lack of store scoping, the terminal capability remains changing prices and voiding transactions at any store during the token-validity window.
